# AGENTS.md

Kaioken is a terminal-based AI coding assistant that combines an interactive chat agent with a knowledge engine. The single most important thing to know before editing is that the agent will not make any state-changing modifications (like editing files) without explicit user approval via the TUI.

## Commands
- `make test`: Run all unit tests (`go test ./... -count=1` to disable caching)
- `make vet`: Run Go static analysis
- `make lint`: Run golangci-lint if installed (skips if missing)
- `make check`: Run test and vet
- `make build`: Build binary (first `go build ./...`, then `go build -o kaioken.exe ./cmd/kaioken`)
- `make clean`: Remove `kaioken.exe` binary

## Architecture
- CLI entry point: `cmd/kaioken/main.go` defines commands (init, scan, plan, generate, wiki, update, models, status, skills, hook, serve)
- TUI: `internal/tui/tui.go` handles user input/output and forwards messages to agent
- Agent: `internal/agent/agent.go` processes LLM interactions and executes approved tools (file edits, command runs)
- Knowledge engine: `internal/wiki/wiki.go` generates documentation; invoked by `wiki`/`update` commands
- LLM client: `internal/llm/openrouter.go` handles provider communication (OpenRouter, etc.)
- Dependencies flow inward: high-level (cmd, tui) → mid-level (agent, wiki, llm) → utilities (scan, plan, codemap, state, skills, serve, gitx); config is cross-cutting

## Conventions
- State-changing tools (edit_file, run_command, etc.) require explicit TUI approval before execution
- Configuration: global in `$HOME/.config/kaioken/config.yaml`, per-repo in `.kaioken/config.yaml` (per-repo overrides global)
- TUI command palette opened with `/` provides access to slash-commands (e.g., `/wiki`, `/update`)
- Error handling: functions return `error` as last value; callers must check and handle
- Naming: packages match directories; interfaces use `-er` suffix; structs/methods use MixedCaps

## Gotchas
- `.kaioken` directory (config, sessions, skills, generated wiki) is agent-managed; do not edit directly
- `kaioken.exe` is built from source; never commit—use `make build` to compile
- Wiki generation (`kaioken wiki` or `/wiki`) is resource-intensive (multiple LLM calls, high token usage)

messages.content:
The project structure is as follows:

**Root Directory:**
- `.kaioken/` - Agent-managed directory (config, sessions, skills, generated wiki)
- `AGENTS.md` - Agent guidelines and architecture overview
- `KAIOKEN-settings.json` - Application settings
- `Makefile` - Build and test commands
- `PRISM_RAG/` - Subdirectory (possibly related module)
- `cmd/` - CLI entry point (`cmd/kaioken/main.go`)
- `go.mod`, `go.sum` - Go dependency files
- `internal/` - Core application packages
- `kaioken-daemon-temp.exe`, `kaioken.exe`, `kaioken.exe.old` - Executables

**Key Subdirectories:**

**.kaioken/**
- `KNOWLEDGE.md`, `architecture.md` - Documentation
- `config.yaml` - Configuration
- `knowledge/` - Knowledge cards
- `modules.yaml` - Module definitions
- `sessions/` - Session data
- `skills/` - Skill definitions
- `state.json` - Application state
- `wiki/` - Generated wiki documentation
- `wiki_plan.yaml`, `wiki_state.yaml` - Wiki planning and state

**internal/** (core packages):
- `agent/` - Agent core logic
- `tui/` - Terminal User Interface
- `wiki/` - Knowledge engine and wiki generation
- `llm/` - LLM provider integration
- `config/` - Configuration handling
- `scan/` - Repository scanning
- `plan/` - Planning functionality
- `gitx/` - Git extensions
- `session/` - Session management
- `skills/` - Skills system
- `state/` - State management
- `codemap/` - Code mapping and indexing
- `generate/` - Code generation
- `serve/` - Wiki server
- `daemon/` - Daemon functionality
- `memory/` - Memory management
- `plan/` - Planning
- `setup/` - Setup utilities
- `termpty/` - Terminal pty handling
- `version/` - Version information
- `agentsmd/`, `ext/` - Additional modules

**cmd/**:
- `kaioken/` - Main CLI application (`main.go` defines commands: init, scan, plan, generate, wiki, update, models, status, skills, hook, serve)

This structure follows the architecture described in AGENTS.md where dependencies flow inward: high-level (cmd, tui) → mid-level (agent, wiki, llm) → utilities (scan, plan, codemap, state, skills, serve, gitx) with configuration as a cross-cutting concern. The `.kaioken/` directory is agent-managed and should not be edited directly.
